purpose: Compare fixed-hash weight-bank FFNs using DeepGEMM BF16 and NVIDIA TE GroupedLinear on one Hopper
deepgemm_version_reason: Pinned SM90 BF16 implementation uses fmt rather than the std::format required by latest 2.8.2. Host extension builds with C++17; NVCC JIT keeps upstream's C++20 default. This is not a latest-version ranking.
gpu: single complete H100 or H200, at least 40000 MiB for large weight-bank optimizer buffers
optimizer_benchmark: Existing MuonAdamW, independent 2D expert matrices, five NS steps, momentum .95, beta2 .9, LR .005, no weight decay; synthetic VJP updates only
precision: FP32 master weights; BF16 GEMM operands and activations; FP32 reductions internally
correctness: Both implementations versus PyTorch BF16 reference, forward and every input/weight VJP; zero, tiny, odd token counts, empty groups and production dimensions; relative L2 <= 0.02 with absolute floor 1e-7
measurements: complete FFN forward/backward including weight casts and token permutation
timing: warmup then ABBA backend order; CUDA-event and synchronized wall time; compilation excluded and reported separately
scope_limit: Single FFN operator benchmark with synthetic activations and real cached input IDs. No NTP quality claim or full-model throughput claim.
failure_policy: Keep failures and resource skips; no threshold relaxation, automatic resubmission, formal run or automatic production backend switch
correctness_isolation: TE and DeepGEMM each run all five unchanged checks in independent child processes. Only fully passing backends are profiled. Any failed backend keeps the overall report incomplete; no failed check is waived.
te_master_weight_interface: BF16 torch.autocast with cache disabled, FP32 master parameters unchanged.
backward_timing: Fresh forward graph per iteration for both backends, synchronization before backward; forward is excluded from the packed-backward timing. Complete forward/backward and optimizer timing paths unchanged.
